headline: BUY on valuation with low conviction; Q2FY27 results on 7 November are the test
summary: Tata Steel makes flat and long steel products in India and overseas. Q1FY27 revenue rose 14.3% YoY to Rs 60,794 crore (NSE results filing) and profit excluding one-offs rose 17.5% YoY. Provisional Q2FY27 data shows India crude steel production up about 10% YoY to 6.21 million tonnes and sales up 7%. The board meeting for Q2FY27 results was moved from 27 October to 7 November 2026, and the NSE filings confirm that no newer results were published as of 1 November. The model target of Rs 217.1 implies 29.5% upside and is in line with the consensus mean of Rs 217.0; the composite score of 50 sits exactly at the quality gate, and conviction is Low because the DCF value of Rs 51.17 points the other way. Analyst view: the BUY rests on an earnings recovery that consensus prices at 1.9x trailing EPS; with net debt to equity of 0.82x and the price 13.5% below its 200-day average, we would treat it as a low-conviction call until Q2FY27 shows the margin gain in reported profit.
highlights: Q2FY27 (provisional): India crude steel production of 6.21 million tonnes, up about 10% YoY from 5.64 million tonnes and up from 5.76 million tonnes in Q1FY27.
Q2FY27 (provisional): total sales of 5.97 million tonnes, up 7% YoY.
Q1FY27 revenue of Rs 60,794 crore, up 14.3% YoY; EBITDA excluding other income of Rs 9,264 crore, up 24.7% from Rs 7,428 crore in Q1FY26 (NSE results filings).
FY26 net profit was Rs 10,794 crore after a loss of Rs 4,437 crore in FY24; FY24 included one-off charges of Rs 6,639 crore before tax (digest).
35 analysts have a mean target of Rs 217.0 (range Rs 175 to Rs 260), close to the model target of Rs 217.1.
Shareholding on 30-Sep-2026: promoter 32.94% (33.19% a year earlier), FII 18.19%, DII 27.52%; no promoter shares pledged (NSE shareholding pattern).
catalysts: Q2FY27 financial results at the board meeting on 7 November 2026: the first test of whether higher India volumes lift EBITDA.
A sustained move back above the 200-day average of Rs 193.8 would reverse the current downtrend signal.
risks: Netherlands liquid steel production fell to 1.52 million tonnes in Q2FY27 from 1.67 million tonnes a year earlier, so European volumes are still weak.
Analyst view: consensus forward EPS of Rs 17.90 is 1.9x trailing EPS of Rs 9.53 excluding one-offs; the model caps it at 1.4x, but a weaker steel price cycle would still remove most of the upside.
The composite score of 50 is at the quality gate threshold; a score one point lower would cut the rating to HOLD.
Valuation cross-check: the DCF gives Rs 51.17 against a price of Rs 167.6, because the base free cash flow and 3% to 15% growth band do not capture a cyclical recovery.
